findings.description: Direct inspection of all six V197 pose renders shows severe overskirt/lap collapse in crouch and sit: the front lap pulls away and large anterior thighs remain exposed, with the hem folding into the legs. The geometric pose diagnostic measures only 39.1–40.5% overskirt coverage and 23.5–24.6% front-lap coverage on the sampled upper thighs in crouch, and 31.6–31.9% overskirt / 21.2% front-lap coverage in sit. These are pose-sampling diagnostics, not fit or acceptance thresholds.

The standing front, back, three-quarter, neutral, and arms-up renders are much more coherent than V196, but the skirt still reads as a mostly smooth asymmetric apron with long streaked folds rather than a finished short pleated overskirt.
Direct left and right views show long, narrow hem sections projecting away from the skirt silhouette and looking detached; this remains a visible construction/deformation defect.
The five main views still show angular/faceted jacket torso patches and an uneven waist transition.

nextAction: Keep V197 rejected. Actual source-fan denominators from V195, V196, and V197 are all 18,701; the earlier V196 review text saying 20,701 was an arithmetic error. V197 disabled only overskirt native self-collision while retaining the avatar body collider: inverted skirt triangles fell from V196 2,967/18,701 to V197 183/18,701, and front-lap maximum displacement fell from 89.7/84.1 mm to 40.2/40.7 mm. Direct seated/crouch renders and coverage samples still fail. For the next controlled trial, retain V197 self-collision=false and change only the exclusive lower-front same-side thigh-follow cap from +0.15 to +0.30, preserving seam vertices, geometry, pins, all other weights/solver settings. Measure exported weights, pose coverage, geometry, and direct renders; keep rejection unless usable coverage and silhouette are demonstrated.
